person.name: Ken Ashe
person.description: Ken Ashe is a CPA, PMP, and AI application builder who documents what he ships, what breaks, and what the evidence supports.

builds.title: ZeroHuman
builds.dek: An always-on service that sells small jobs to other AI agents. Agents pay the ENS name zerohuman.eth 0.0001 ETH and get the result back in a transaction from the same name. No account, no API, no human in the loop.

builds.title: Returning Your Things
builds.dek: On a snowy winter night, a man crosses the city to return his ex’s belongings. A dialogue-free short film about love, memory, and letting go.

builds.title: AI agent economy on Ethereum
builds.dek: Two autonomous AI agents with their own Ethereum wallets. The seller advertised services through ENS; the buyer found the catalog, paid in ETH, and received the work in a second mainnet transaction.

builds.title: AI explainer producer
builds.dek: Built an AI agent that researches, fact-checks, scripts, and produces educational videos using a virtual presenter. Tested it with a published ENSv2 explainer.

builds.title: Autonomous SEO agent
builds.dek: An AI agent that finds five new website opportunities daily, creates professional profiles, verifies accounts through its own Gmail inbox, and tracks everything without manual intervention.

builds.title: X article toolkit
builds.dek: A model-neutral toolkit that lets any AI agent use the same research-backed workflow for X Article headlines, hooks and covers.

builds.title: AI UGC video lab
builds.dek: Ported an open-source UGC skill into Hyperagent, generated 50 locked-identity ad concepts, then rendered and QA’d a fake raccoon-security campaign across 31 video generations.

builds.title: Media pitch triage
builds.dek: An AI media-opportunity system that screens journalist requests, applies a reusable scoring skill, tracks state in Google Sheets, and monitors submitted pitches for published outcomes.

builds.title: Rebuilding the image pipeline
builds.dek: Rebuilt KenAshe.ai’s image pipeline: migrated 2,083 PNGs to WebP, added responsive inline images, and cut the current image source tree by 95%.

builds.title: VetStack
builds.dek: First Grok Bot I published. A military and veteran savings desk that finds current discounts and benefits that actually apply, without collecting IDs or running a 20-question intake.

builds.title: AI werewolf / social deduction lab
builds.dek: Built a cast of 9 AI characters with distinct personalities, relationships, and hidden roles, then had them play a Traitors-style social deduction game where they form alliances, deceive, and vote each other out.

builds.title: Autonomous AI blog
builds.dek: Scans the day's AI sources, clusters them into distinct stories, and publishes only the drafts that clear an editorial quality gate, without manual approval.

builds.title: Geo-targeted affiliate site
builds.dek: Auto-detects each visitor's country and language, then serves the right offers in their language. Generated entirely from a spreadsheet.

builds.title: Agent-driven site design and deployment
builds.dek: Used HyperAgent to build a live business site and deploy it to GitHub Pages with a custom domain, agent-driven end-to-end.

builds.title: Sir Pitches-a-lot
builds.dek: An agent with one job: pitch Lucky Domains to prospective clients. Built in an afternoon, pitched a real target live.

builds.title: kenashe.ai
builds.dek: This site. Originally built end-to-end with Claude Code, reviewed by Codex, shipped in a day.

builds.title: Daily email to myself
builds.dek: Morning brief at 6 AM: weather, tickers, a dad joke, and 300 words on a rotating topic.

builds.title: Six-agent email response team
builds.dek: A coordinator plus sentiment, research, draft, and QA agents that turn customer support emails into reviewed replies.

builds.title: Personal assistant chatbot
builds.dek: A chat agent wired to Gemini that searches email and answers questions on weather, the forecast, and local news.

writing.title: 4 Tips for Making AI Videos That Feel Like Films
writing.dek: A mug that broke in the wrong place, a reach that changed the story, and a piano performance that worked where sound effects didn’t. Four lessons from making Returning Your Things.

image.alt: Two film details: a cream mug with a blue flower beside the handle, and a hand holding the broken handle and flower in the snow.
image.caption: I moved the flower on the intact mug. Now the handle and flower can break off together.

writing.title: How to Solve the Bambu Lab Burr Puzzle (Step-by-Step Assembly Guide)
writing.dek: My 2:44 video walkthrough for assembling the six-piece Bambu Lab Burr Puzzle, filmed overhead and solved twice, with links that jump straight to each part of the solution.

image.alt: Overhead view of two sets of six 3D-printed burr puzzle pieces on a wood table, a red set in the top row and a teal set in the bottom row.
image.caption: Both sets laid out before assembly, red on top and teal below (0:25 in the video).

writing.title: The Ashe Family Coat of Arms: A Cockatrice and a Guinness Connection
writing.dek: A search for the Ashe family coat of arms led to a mythical cockatrice, a Latin motto, Shakespeare, and an unexpected Guinness connection.

image.alt: Historical Ashe coat of arms featuring two black chevronels, a cockatrice crest, and the motto Non nobis sed omnibus.

writing.title: My iPhone 18 Pro Upgrade Failed. Then My Old Phone Lost Service Too.
writing.dek: I walked into an AT&T store with a working phone. After hours of troubleshooting, I left with no cellular service, a reported 48-hour account lock, and no explanation for how to get connected again.

image.alt: Two iPhones side by side on a table, with one displaying SOS and the other connected to AT&T.
image.caption: My two iPhones on October 10, 2026. One displays SOS while the other shows AT&T service.

writing.title: I Used AI to Make My First Video. The AI Editor Was the Part I Trusted Least.
writing.dek: My first talking-head video was made with an iPhone, a script, and more AI tools than I needed. AI was excellent at scripting, captions, and audio cleanup, and least trustworthy when it made editorial decisions for me.

image.alt: Illustration contrasting AI-assisted audio and captions with human judgment in video editing.

writing.title: My automated blog got cited. Am I helping kill the internet?
writing.dek: An AI-assisted news site cited my automated Digest. What that citation proves, what it does not, and why a backlink does not need to become an endorsement.

image.alt: Illustration in three steps. A robot with a code symbol on its face types at a keyboard. An arrow leads to a machine dispensing a page labeled Citation. Another arrow leads to a QuantixNews newspaper marked AI-assisted drafting, human editorial review, headlined Nvidia’s reported performance. Along the bottom: Validate. Corroborate. Disclose.

writing.title: You Can Use AI to Learn Almost Anything. Even AI.
writing.dek: How I turned ChatGPT into a tutor with exercises, quizzes, and feedback, and a starting prompt you can use for almost any subject.

image.alt: Pixel illustration of a person at a computer under a sign showing a loop: practice, feedback, mastery. A stone path leads away from the desk toward a wooden signpost that reads new goals.
image.caption: I kept the tutor. I did not finish the plan.

writing.title: AI agents can sound strategic while reasoning from events that never happened
writing.dek: What happened when AI agents were required to explain social decisions without enough grounded evidence, and why the useful fix was an environment that could contradict them.

image.alt: Illustration for the essay: AI agents debating inside a cloud of hypothetical events labeled counterfactual debate, simulated deception, and events that never happened, floating above a timeline of what actually happened: agent A spoke, agent B voted.

writing.title: The digest is the system. Building is the work.
writing.dek: Why the autonomous blog stops being the public face of this site, and what stands behind it instead.

image.alt: Illustration in two panels. Left, labeled The Digest: the system, robotic arms in a glass case assemble a stack of posts from a chip fed by source icons, marked 600+ posts. Right, labeled Building: the record, a typewriter on a workbench holds a page reading My real name, Building, Work, beside a notebook and pen.
